set.body:
Journey: See. Track: console.

Outcome
Opening a study shows one page that answers: what is this, who holds it, what does it contain, what state is it in, and what can I do.

Acceptance
1. Header: title and description from the catalog record (SEE2), custodian and stewards by name, licence, current release and its date, and status (private, shared with N people, listed, published with a DOI). Until SEE2 lands, read the title from dataset_description.json.
2. Grid: participants by data type (anat, func, dwi, fmap, eeg, meg, beh, physio and eye-tracking, phenotype, other), with sessions expandable. Each cell shows presence and the coverage level (assessed, described, preserved), with a legend. A study of 60 participants and two sessions reads well at desktop width and stays usable at 390 px.
3. Choosing a cell opens the existing file inspector filtered to that participant and data type.
4. Summary counts: participants, sessions, files, size, and findings that need attention. When sourcedata/sanctity/intake.json is present, an Origin line shows the source system, the number of sessions and the converter and mapping versions.
5. Actions shown by permission: Add data, Share, Publish, Download. A reader without rights sees no dead buttons.
6. Steward and custodian names come from the API. Add a small read if none returns them today.
7. Built as its own module from the SEE1 specimen. Compute the grid from the release inventory. Add a server-side coverage read only if a 10,000-entry release takes more than one second to render.

Not in scope
Editing from the grid. Views across studies. Charts.

Start from
- modules/http/src/main/scala/sanctity/http/PublicJson.scala line 28: every entry carries its group and coverage level.
- modules/http/src/main/resources/sanctity/ui/coverage.js and app.js, releaseView.

Evidence
Console behaviour checks for the grid. A screenshot that matches the approved specimen. The SEE8 rehearsal.
